messages.content: Maintain a 2:1 ratio of declarative to interrogative sentences in your response. Show a metric space (M, d) is complete if and only if any sequence (F_n) of nonempty closed subsets of M with - F_{n+1} \subset F_n - diam F_n \rightarrow 0 as n \rightarrow \infty has a nonempty intersection

message.content: Let (F_n) be a nested sequence of nonempty closed subsets of M with diameters tending to zero. Completeness is equivalent to the common intersection of the F_n being nonempty. The forward direction uses the completeness property and the shrinking of diameters. The reverse direction follows from the nonempty intersection condition for such sequences. Are both directions covered? Is the proof now complete?
